## Zip 52: the audit fuzz's "$5 short" (🎾52.fuzz), Mon Nov 16, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-j2knq5` (the session is named "🎾52.fuzz"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `3dd6468`, then main `e2aad07` (Zip 51b, the Money change note, deployed at 11:29 AM) merged in. Zips 48 to 51b
live). MOVES MONEY (Unmark and the player's own "Didn't pay?" on a paid seat). No schema change, no Cloudflare variable, no switch, no wording or
look change.

### What the fuzz saw
- The fuzz is tests/audit-r4.test.ts "random sequences" (a unit test against the real server code, not a browser test). On the old code its
  finalize-heavy half failed about 1 sequence in 100 (seeds 1020, 3073, 4020, 4061 in 400 tried; the default run has 40, so about 1 run in 3).
  Every failure: "more credit than price" on a played seat, after an Unmark that answered 409.
- The steps (seed 4020, as plain steps): Emery's $14 is marked paid. She drops out: her $14 becomes credit. She comes back in (her own I'm in, or
  Alex's Add): the $14 credit goes on the seat, which reads Paid. 6 play, final price $9: Finalize gives her $5 back as credit. Alex taps Unmark
  on her payment: refused ("already used the credit from this game"), and yet her credit went from $5 to $0 while the seat still kept all $14.
  So the screens said: Players tab and her phone: credit $0; the game: Emery Paid $14; it should have been credit $5, Paid $9.
  (At 5, 8 or 10 played the loss is $3, $7 or $9: always the money back from Finalize.)

### Cause
- Unmark takes back, in one batch, the credit that came back from the payment, then marks the seat unpaid. Since Zip 49 (Nov 15) there are two
  kinds: the money back from Finalize, and a "trim" (a guest's share given back from a seat that stays paid: Remove guest, a late pair, a host
  back alone). Each take-back checked on its own that the player's credit still covered it. When the credit covered the Finalize money but not
  both, the Finalize money was taken back, the trim was not, and so the "unpaid" step (which needs both gone) was refused: the tap said no, the
  seat stayed paid, and the money already taken was gone. The opposite order, or a Finalize or Reopen landing in the same instant, did the same.
- Why the fuzz hit it: its clock does not move between taps, so the drop and the rejoin happen in the same millisecond, and the $14 from the
  drop reads as a "trim" of the new payment. On the live site that needs two taps in the same millisecond (not a real case), BUT a real trim
  does the same: Guest spot is on live, so: Blair pays $28 for herself and a guest, Remove guest ($14 back), 6 play ($5 back, $19 credit), she
  spends $14 of it on the next game, then Alex taps Unmark on the first game: $5 gone. Proven on the old code (tests/zip52-fuzzfix.test.ts,
  first test, real clock).
- Live (read only, `wrangler d1 execute` SELECT, no names): not one credit entry has ever been taken back by an Unmark or a Reopen
  (no "undone" entries at all), so no live game shows the problem.

### Fix (server/credit.ts undoSeatBackStatements, used by server/admin.ts applyPayment's Unmark)
- One function makes both take-backs, each with the same check: the credit covers BOTH together (beyond a pending cash out), the seat is still
  paid and not settled, and the game is still the finalize the screen read. That is exactly what the "unpaid" step needs, so all three go in
  together or nothing moves. A refused Unmark now moves nothing (the 409 message is the same as before).
- Left as it is (a note): with the fake clock, a drop and a rejoin in the same millisecond still make the drop's credit read as a trim, so that
  Unmark is refused ("already used the credit") with nothing moved. On live it would need both taps in the same millisecond.

### A second, older gap the fuzz found once the first was fixed (seeds 11036 and 15002; both fail the same way on the old code)
- Seed 15002 as plain steps: 10 in. Finalize with 9 played ($6) before Harper paid; Alex marks her paid: $6 cash. Reopen. Finalize with 6
  played ($9): her $6 is held on the seat, she owes $3. Reopen. Finalize with 9 played ($6): the $6 held pays the seat. Alex taps Unmark: the
  seat read "unpaid" while the $6 on it already covered the $6 price, so it owed nothing, read unpaid, and that $6 could never come back.
  Seed 11036 is the same with $3 credit + $8 cash at $7 (the $3 went back, the $8 sat on an unpaid seat).
- Cause: Unmark with no new cash on top of what the seat already held gives the credit back and marks the seat unpaid, but only an Unmark WITH
  new cash on top then checked whether what stays on the seat still covers the price. Fix (server/admin.ts applyPayment, `stays`): the same
  check runs whenever anything stays on the seat: it is paid with it, and anything above the final price comes back as credit.
- On live this needs Mark paid, then Reopen and Finalize twice with different counts, then Unmark: rare, no stuck seat seen (the integrity
  checks do not look for this one; see the report).

### Tests
- tests/zip52-fuzzfix.test.ts (13; the last 2 are the second gap, both fail on the old code): the real-clock Guest spot case (Unmark refused, Blair keeps her $5, nothing moved); the same with the credit
  back in the pot (one Unmark takes back $5 and $14, seat owes again); the fuzz shape at 5, 6, 8 and 10 played, back in by her own I'm in and by
  Alex's Add (nothing lost, then Reopen and Finalize again give the same money back once); a plain Unmark after Finalize unchanged; seed
  15002's and seed 11036's shapes (Harper stays Paid $6; Indy gets her $3 back, the $8 pays the seat, $1 back). 11 of the 13 fail on the old code.
- tests/audit-r4.test.ts: the ids the server makes now follow the seed, so a failing seed replays exactly (`FUZZ_FROM=<seed> FUZZ_FIN_SEQS=1`);
  each Finalize step logs who played.
- Review fix (fresh reviewer): a seat paid only by cash held from an earlier Finalize that covers its price, no credit, no new cash, no trim
  credit: Unmark now answers "nothing changed" and writes no History line (before this zip it left the seat stuck unpaid; with only the `stays`
  fix it said "changed" and wrote "marked unpaid" while the seat stayed Paid).
- Fresh reviewer (independent): nothing blocking. Checked the SQL (numbering, aliases, one read per statement), that the take-backs happen if and
  only if the seat goes unpaid, a pending cash out (409, nothing moves), the self path, refused Unmarks (ledger unchanged), guest seats, did-not-play
  seats, games not finalized; ran the 43 test files that touch Unmark or "Didn't pay?" (1,187 passed, 1 skipped). Its SHOULD FIX (an Unmark
  that cannot take off cash held from an earlier Finalize) is the question for Alex below; its trim note is fixed.

### Proof
- Fuzz: 30 runs in a row with different seeds (FUZZ_FROM 51000 to 80000, each run 40 finalize-heavy + 60 mixed sequences): 30 of 30 clean,
  3,000 sequences, about 90,000 book checks. Runs 7 to 30 on the merged code (with Zip 51b); runs 1 to 6 on the same fix just before the merge.
  An earlier 15 runs (seeds 11000 to 25000, which hold both "credit stuck" seeds) were clean on the fix before the review fix. Old code, same
  test: 4 failures in 400 finalize-heavy sequences (random ids) and seeds 11036, 15002 with the seeded ids.
- Audit C probes (guest, late fee, venue; copied in and deleted after): 114 of 127 on both main and this branch, the same 13 (old answers Zips
  49 and 51 changed on purpose).
- Browser: e2e/zip49.cjs 33 of 33, e2e/zip51.cjs 16 of 16 (no screen changed in this zip, so one run each).

### Question for Alex
- Unmark only ever takes off the LATEST cash. Once a Reopen and a new Finalize have turned a Mark paid into cash held on the seat, Unmark can no
  longer take it off (it now says nothing changed). Is that what you want, or should Unmark be able to take that cash off too?

### What was wrong

### The new rule (one rule for everyone, server/needsCard.ts)

## Zip 55: Tournaments, piece 1 (🎾55.tourney1), Tue Nov 17, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-yjbe3g` (the session is named "🎾55.tourney1"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `166d368` (Zip 54
live). New switch **TOURNAMENTS**, ships OFF. **Database change: migration `0023_tournaments` (three NEW tables).** Applied to the fake preview
database only; NOT on live: waiting for Alex's "ship it" (STOP RULE). No money moves: the ticket price and the champion credit are only stored.
Pieces 2 (tickets, waitlist), 3 (teams, game day, End tournament) and 4 (tie wheel, final) are NOT built.

### What it does
1. Tables (`migrations/0023_tournaments.sql`, additive only, every foreign key ON DELETE CASCADE so a restore, a re-seed or Remove player can never
   fail because of them): `tournaments` (name, size, courts, minutes, start, ticket_cents, champion_credit_cents, offered_dates, final_date, status,
   visibility me/all, times; one open tournament per group by a partial unique index), `tournament_signups` (player, status in/out, picked_level,
   approved_level, dates, joined_at; one row per player per tournament, kept after a back out), `tournament_level_history` (every level a player
   picked and every level the organizer set, per tournament, never edited). Later pieces will add `tournament_tickets`, `tournament_teams`,
   `tournament_games` next to them; status has no CHECK so they need no table rebuild.
   (Pass 3, before shipping: `tournaments` also has `format` ('doubles' or 'americano', default 'doubles') and `second_credit_cents`
   (Americano's 2nd place, default 0), at the end of the table in 0023 itself; 0023 has never shipped, so no 0024.)
2. Create tournament (Settings > Schedule; `src/pages/admin/Tournament.tsx`): the mocks' cards (03, 01, 02, 24): name, Dates to offer (a
   scrollable calendar from this month, opening on next month after the 15th; tap to light; "N LIT"), Start time / Ends, Players expected 6/8/10/12
   with each size's court plans (BEST first; 2.5 and 3 hour plans only while Booking hours is on for everyone, else dimmed with the mock's note),
   Champion prize (credit $14, $0 allowed, total for 2 winners), Ticket price ($16, the same for every size), What players see, Who can see it
   (Only me first), "Open sign-up (only me)". It opens as a full-height sheet (title bar and ✕), like Edit game.
3. Players (`src/tournament/TournamentHome.tsx`, its own download): the pinned ticket card (states 1 and 2 of mock 08 and the Date picked look:
   DATE PICKED, the date on the stub, "Tickets open soon", VOTE done and TICKETS next), the 2-step Sign up sheet (level, then dates; the mock's
   words), "You're on the list", See who's signed up (names only), Edit my sign-up (level and dates), Back out? (Stay signed up / Yes, back out).
   Before the date is picked the stub shows "DATE TBD DEC–JAN 7:30 PM" (the months on offer). After it is picked a new sign-up (or an edit) can
   only pick that date. (Alex's feedback took the level note and the prize line off the sign-up sheets, and the "What players see" card off Create.)
4. The organizer's tournament page (from the Home card's Levels / Pick the date, or Settings > Schedule): Who can see it, the level list of mock 14
   (name, "Picked 3.6", the level, a pencil; the sheet tints the player's pick "SAGE PICKED" and boxes the organizer's "YOUR PICK"; Save 3.4), the
   offered dates with how many can play each (the most-picked count in bold), tap one to see who can and cannot, Pick it, or Take back the date;
   Settings (Edit); Cancel tournament. History gets a line for each step and each player's sign-up, edit and back out.
5. Only me (`server/tournament.ts` `visibleTo`): only the organizer's own player on a phone signed in with the real PIN (or the organizer's View
   as of their own player) sees the card and the "Only you can see this" strip (mock 04, Show to everyone with a confirm). Anyone else, including
   a phone that only picked the organizer's name and a read-only PIN helper: no `tournament` key in `/api/group`, the same change fingerprint as
   with no tournament, and every player route answers 404 "This tournament is not open." (the same for none, off and Only me).
6. Preview test page (`src/pages/admin/TournamentTest.tsx`, `server/tournamentTest.ts`): organizer Home (first row) and Settings > Schedule,
   "Tournament test": Sign-up open, Date picked, No tournament (each also turns the Tournaments row back on), Who can see it, View as each fixed
   name (`/?as=Name`) or Admin. Built only into a preview (`__PREVIEW_BUILD__`, set by `npm run deploy:preview`; `tests/zip55-build.test.ts`
   checks a live build has none of it); the server half answers Not found unless PREVIEW_CALM is on (only previews). The route's address is in
   the live View as copy's file (it runs the server's own code), where it also answers Not found.

### The switch
`TOURNAMENTS`: Settings > Feature switches > "Tournaments" (top row), a kill switch allowed unless "off" (no wrangler.toml line, Zip 45's rule),
the private link `?tournaments=on` (X-Tournaments). Off: no new key in any answer, no new fingerprint segment, the switch read answered by the
shared switch read (no extra trip), the new tables never read. docs/FEATURE_SWITCHES.md has the row.

### Where it differs from the brief (the code is the truth)
- No TEST SPEED RULES section exists in SITE_RULES (neither copy); the usual full unit and browser runs were used.
- Kai is not one of the preview's fixed names (the seed refuses any other name), so the test page uses the 10 fixed names only.
- The kill switch has no wrangler.toml line (Zip 45: allowed-unless-off switches have none); "off" is added only to pull it.
- The stub cannot show "THU 17 DEC" before a date is picked: it shows DATE TBD and the months on offer.
- "Date picked" kicker reads DATE PICKED (state 3's TICKETS OPEN would contradict "Tickets open soon").
- 8-player plan words follow the Create screen (mock 03); the other sizes follow mocks 01 and 02.
- The tournament tables are not in the backup FILE yet (BACKUP_LEFT_OUT; Time Travel keeps them; docs/RESTORE.md says so).
- Create and the tournament page are full-height sheets (with a way back), not a page with no back button.
- The ticket price stays editable after Create in piece 1 (nothing is sold); the Edit screen's note says "before tickets open".
- Only me is decided from the same single read as "is a tournament open?" (`activeTournamentForPlayer`), so any player other than the
  organizer's own costs exactly the trips of "none open", whether the organizer's player is saved by id or matched by the Settings name.

### Review
A fresh reviewer (no part in the build) read the whole change: no Only me leak in any answer, stamp or error, no authorization hole. Its real
findings were fixed in `afddf2a` with a test each: a day that has passed is no longer a choice (players and the date pick); a player's new level
pick goes back to be reviewed (the same pick keeps the organizer's level; the history keeps every step); a level-only edit sends no dates;
every organizer save is guarded so a canceled tournament never comes back; Edit settings keeps a 2.5 or 3 hour plan after Booking hours is
turned off; a second Sign up tap with the same answers writes nothing; the Only me path costs no extra read for a normal player; History says
how many players lost a picked date.

A second review (3 independent reviewers, each finding checked by a separate skeptic who tried to refute it): 12 findings, 7 confirmed, all
fixed in `bf2050d` with a test each (unit, plus browser checks K and L):
- Only me: a phone that merely picked the organizer's name (organizer matched by name, or a saved id of a removed player) cost 1 or 2 extra
  reads while Only me was open (a timing tell, no data). The sign-in check now comes first: such a phone is refused with no extra trip.
- A date pick and an Edit settings save landing at the same moment could leave the picked date outside the offered dates. Both now re-check
  in the same statement ("look again" otherwise).
- Edit settings trimmed players' dates from an earlier read, so a player's own edit in between was lost. The trim now runs on the rows as they
  are, in the same batch. A player's sign-up or edit lands only while the tournament is as it was read (date pick, Edit or Cancel in between:
  "look again").
- History's lost-date count included hidden players. Now only players on the level list.
- A picked date that has passed was still open for sign-up. Now never.
- Every offered date passed, none picked: players had a Sign up that could not work. Now no Sign up, the card says "The dates offered have
  passed.", Edit hides the empty calendar, and the organizer's date card says "Every date you offered has passed. Tap Edit below to offer new
  ones." (Edit with new dates opens it again.)
- A sheet left open kept a date that had closed, so every Save failed. Sheets now drop closed dates.
Refuted (not changed): a player tap racing Cancel (now guarded anyway), saving the same organizer level twice (two lines, as tapped), an Edit
with no change still writing a History line (as before), a level change after the date is picked replacing dates (by design), and a passed
picked date that can be taken back (the organizer's choice).

### Cost (in-process server, 10 players, trips per answer)
| | Player screen | 5-second check |
|---|---|---|
| Switch OFF (as main) | 52 | 23 |
| ON, no tournament | 54 | 24 |
| ON, Only me (any other player) | 54 | 24 |
| ON, Everyone, 3 signed up | 56 | 25 |
OFF adds nothing (the switch read rides the shared switch read). Server time per answer stayed within noise (about 1 to 6 ms here).

## Zip 56: Tournaments, piece 2: tickets (🎾56.tourney2), Tue Nov 17 to Wed Nov 18, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-16mfmv` (the session is named "🎾56.tourney2"). Built on main `beb1aad` (Zip 55 live, TOURNAMENTS OFF). The same
switch, TOURNAMENTS, and the per-tournament Who can see it. **Money moves. Database change: migration `0024_tournament_tickets` (one NEW table,

changes after testing piece 1 on live (A to G below); they replace parts of the brief and are built in.

### The database change (the brief: show Alex the exact change first)
`ALTER TABLE tournaments ADD COLUMN pay_by TEXT;` (when ticket money is due; set when the date is picked, which opens tickets) and a new table
`tournament_tickets`: one row per player per tournament (`UNIQUE (tournament_id, player_id)`, both foreign keys ON DELETE CASCADE): `place`
('spot', 'line' or 'none'), `place_at` (the order of the line and of the spots), `price_cents` ($0 for the organizer), `credit_cents` (credit
used on it), `paid_cents` (cash the organizer confirmed), `claim_cents` and `claim_at` (an I paid waiting), `paid_at`, `created_at`,
`updated_at`; checks: never more on a ticket than its price, a spot only when paid in full; two triggers refuse a 13th spot ("tournament_full");
an index on player_id. Additive only: old code never reads it. Undo: `DROP TABLE tournament_tickets;` and `ALTER TABLE tournaments DROP
COLUMN pay_by;` (only with no tickets sold). Alex's changes needed NO further table or column.

### Alex's changes after testing piece 1 (built in)

  setting: two days before at 7:00 PM (Tuesday for a Thursday), changeable. A tournament whose date was picked before this (piece 1 on live)

- C. The smart plan (organizer only: a Plan card on the tournament page, the Plan line and "Your cost if it fills" on the Home card): L = players
  locked in; planned size = L rounded up to even, plus 2, 6 to 12; 6 = 1 court 2.5 hours, 8 = 2 courts 2 hours, 10 = 2 courts 2.5 hours, 12 = 2
  courts 3 hours (each size's best plan). Players see "N of the planned size"; every spot is taken only at 12, then the waitlist. The plan's
  start and hours are what players see (7:30 PM; 7:00 PM for the 3 hour plan). Cost = the court ($24 an hour a court) minus the tickets ((planned
  size - 1) x the price if it fills; N x the price paid now) plus the winners' credits (Locked doubles 2 x the champion credit; Americano 1st
  plus 2nd); "Your cost if it fills $12", small "With 5 paid now $44"; when the tickets more than cover it, "-$4". A 2.5 or 3 hour plan

### What it does
1. Picking the date (organizer, the tournament page) opens tickets: the flat price ($16 to start, the same at any size, never from the court
   cost), Pay by as above. Once players may hold tickets (tickets open on Everyone, or a player other than the organizer has a ticket, also
   after a Reschedule) the price and format stay, and Who can see it stays Everyone. The organizer's own seat is a $0 ticket and one of the
   spots, taken at once when they are on the list.
2. Players (pictures 07 to 12): Tickets open, "Lock my spot · $16" and See who's in; tapping the card opens the overlay (Who's in N of the
   planned size, their own row "Pay to lock in", Open spot rows). Lock my spot uses their credit at once (the site's rule at I'm in); what is
   left opens the site's own Pay sheet (Pay Alex $16, Venmo, Copy Venmo, I paid). I paid waits for the organizer like a game's I paid ("Paid ·
   Waiting for Alex to confirm"): it holds no spot. Paid in full with money that counts (credit, or cash the organizer confirmed) = locked in.
3. Waitlist (after 12): "12 spots taken", Join waitlist, then "Hold my spot · $16" (pay to hold) or "Just keep me on the list". When a spot
   opens (a back out or Take off), the first PAID person in line (in the order they joined it) gets it by itself; unpaid people stay in line.
   Players see the line by name only (Alex's answer 5); Alex's Tickets list shows Paid or Not paid.
4. Back out after paying (picture 13b's words plus "Your $16 comes back as credit."): credit used goes back to the pot, cash becomes one credit
   entry, the spot opens and the line fills it. An I paid still waiting comes back as credit when the organizer answers it. From the start of
   the night (7:00 PM on the date) a ticket holder cannot back out ("Ask Alex"), and the organizer cannot take anyone off, mark anyone paid or
   move Pay by (those taps are not offered then).
5. The organizer: the amber "Vic tapped I paid ($16), not confirmed." card on Home (Paid / Didn't pay), "Tickets: 6 of 8 locked in" on Home,
   the Tickets list on the tournament page (locked in and how they paid, the waitlist, the list with no ticket; a row opens Paid / Didn't pay,
   Mark paid for cash in hand, Take off the list), the Plan card. Odd number locked in once Pay by has passed: "7 locked in. Need 1 more or 1
   less." on the card; nobody is ever taken off by the site.
6. Cancel or reschedule (picture 30, each with an Are you sure): Cancel gives every paid ticket back as credit at once (one batch with the
   cancel), the organizer's card says Canceled ("Every paid ticket came back as credit."), the players who were on the list see a plain Canceled
   card ("Canceled. Your $16 is back as credit.") for 7 days (never past the date). Reschedule goes back to the date step: the list stays,
   everyone's dates are cleared ("Rescheduled. Pick your dates again"), every ticket keeps its money and its place; anyone can back out for
   credit; picking a new date opens tickets again. Neither is possible once the night is over (10:00 PM): a played night is never refunded,
   and Cancel or reschedule is not offered then. Players keep the Tickets closed card (piece 1's rule: the card stays after the date).
7. A hold that never got a spot: once the night is over (10:00 PM on the date), the first screen that reads the tournament gives it back as
   credit by the same rules (credit to the pot, cash as a credit entry "back from the Winter Classic (no spot opened)"), once.
8. Credit history (player and organizer): "$16 used for the Winter Classic", "$16 back from the Winter Classic (you backed out)", "(taken off
   the list)", "(canceled)", "(no spot opened)", "$10 returned from the Winter Classic (off the list)". With the switch off for that phone the
   entries say "a tournament" (no name). History lines for every tap.
9. Preview test page: Sign-up open, Date picked (tickets open, nobody paid), Tickets open (6 paid), All locked in (10 names, 10 of 12), 7 locked
   in after Pay by, Canceled, Rescheduled, No tournament; each in Locked doubles or Americano (real money rows on the fake database; the books
   read zero at each).

### Where the money is
- Credit used on a ticket: `credit_ledger` 'used' rows, reason `tour:<tournament id>`, no game (like Zip 31's extra time). Back to the pot by
  ending the rows ('dropped' for a back out or Take off, 'canceled' for a cancel or an unused hold).
- Cash: on the ticket (`paid_cents`), only once the organizer confirms. When it comes back it becomes ONE 'kept' credit entry, reason
  `tour:<id>:back|off|cancel|unused` (for an answer to an I paid, worked out in SQL when the answer lands).
- Every money statement works out its amounts inside the database from the rows as they are, guarded by the ticket as it was read, in one
  batch with the change that causes it: a double tap, a refresh, a second phone or a retry finds nothing left to do. Back out and Take off
  always run the money-back statements, so a Lock that lands in between still comes back.
- Books: `scripts/integrity-checks-tournament.sql` (10 checks and one to-do, read-only; a separate file so the older checks still run on a
  database before 0024). The old `scripts/integrity-checks.sql` reads all zeros too.

### Where it differs from the brief (the code is the truth)
- Alex's changes A to G replace the brief's Open tickets step, players expected and the court plan (above).
- First PAID in line means paid in full with money that counts (credit or confirmed cash), in the order they JOINED the line (not the order
  they paid). An I paid still waiting holds nothing, for Lock my spot and for Hold my spot alike.
- The rules use the whole night, 7:00 to 10:00 PM on the date, whatever the plan (the plan moves with the players): ticket taps stop at 7:00 PM,
  and an unused hold comes back after 10:00 PM, done by the first screen that reads the tournament (no clock job; until then it stays on the
  ticket, and the books are right either way).
- A played night (after 10:00 PM) cannot be canceled or rescheduled (that would refund it), so it stays open until game day (piece 3) ends it:
  Create says "A tournament is already open." and players keep its Tickets closed card. A question below.
- Only me: picking the date opens tickets there too (Alex's rule has no exception), but only the organizer can see them (above).
- Picture 29 has no Edit: the tournament's name opens its page. The evens warning shows only after Pay by has passed.
- Sign-up open and Rescheduled keep piece 1's Home card (the format now one line) with a short Plan line added.
- The Canceled card shows for 7 days (never past the date) and only to players who were on the list.
- Reschedule clears everyone's picked dates (they pick again); picking a new date opens tickets again with a new Pay by.
- Pictures 13 and 13b are piece 1's sheets; the back out words add "Your $16 comes back as credit." when the ticket holds money.
- The ticket-stage cards (pictures 07 to 12, and 29) show the one-line format under the name (Alex's answer 6; not drawn).
- Picture 11's Paid / Not paid next to names is on Alex's screen only (Alex's answer 5).
- The cost: "minus the champion credits" is read as the credits adding to the organizer's cost (he pays them out): court, minus tickets, plus
  credits. 6 locked in: 2 courts for 2 hours $96, minus 7 x $16 = $112, plus 2 x $14 = $28: $12. The free seat is always taken off (Alex's
  rule), also when the organizer is not on the list.
- A piece 1 date pick opens tickets the first time any screen reads it: a player's 5-second check counts, and so does a phone with the private
  tournaments link while the switch is off for everyone.

   closed). From Pay by on (`ticketPhase`): no new Lock my spot, no Join waitlist, no I paid from a player with no place. Exception, a spot
   freed by a back out (or the organizer's Take off) after Pay by: the first PAID waitlist player gets it by itself (as before); with nobody

### Known limits (from the fresh reviewer; no money is ever affected)
- The freed-spot count is "spots freed since Pay by minus spots taken since Pay by". An organizer Mark paid (or confirming an I paid that was
  tapped before Pay by) after Pay by also counts as a spot taken, so it can use up one freed spot early.
- Two buyers tapping Lock at the same instant for one freed spot can both get a spot while spots are open; a buyer with only part credit holds
  no place, so a second buyer can also start. Nobody loses money: unused credit stays on the ticket and comes back on Back out or at 10:00 PM.
- A player already in line may still Lock or Hold after Pay by (they were on the waitlist before it).
- Restore on a tournament canceled more than 7 days ago works, but its Canceled card does not come back to Home (the 7 day window, Zip 56).
- Fixed after the review: a paid place in line or an I paid waiting keeps its card in the last 3 hours; a Pay by in an earlier month (a game on
  the 1st) shows the full card from that month.

## Zip 60: Players vote the format (🎾60.formatvote), Wed Nov 18, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-hnlsro` (the session is named "🎾60.formatvote"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `cbf7272` (Zip 59 live, TOURNAMENTS OFF). Same switch, TOURNAMENTS, and the per-tournament Who can see it. **Database change: migration `0025_format_vote` (two NEW nullable columns, no default, no backfill):** `tournament_signups.format_vote` and `tournaments.format_source`. Applied to the fake preview database only. **NOT on live: waiting for Alex's "ship it".**

### What it does (the brief's six things)
1. Create and Edit have a third format choice, "Let players vote", the default for a new tournament. Locked doubles and Americano work as before. Stored as `format_source = 'vote'` with the placeholder format 'doubles' (the `format` column has a CHECK that allows only 'doubles' and 'americano', and no table rebuild was allowed). The prize card in vote mode shows "Winner or 1st place" and "2nd place".
2. While the vote is open (vote source, no date locked, and no player holds a ticket) the player card's format line reads "Tournament style TBD" and the stub says "~7:30 PM"; the track shows Vote, Tickets, Games. The organizer's card says "Format: players vote".
3. Sign-up step 2 and Edit sign-up: under the dates, "Format you'd like" with three rows in the level list's row style (Locked doubles / same partner all night, Americano / new partner every round, Either is fine, preselected). Only while the vote is open; Edit can change it until the date is locked. A vote sent after that is ignored.
4. Pick date (`lockDate` in server/tournament.ts) counts the votes of players on the list (active, not backed out) who picked that date, Either for neither side. Majority wins. A tie or no sides: the first tournament ever is Locked doubles, otherwise the OPPOSITE of the most recent earlier tournament that is not canceled and had a decided format. The rule is the pure function `decideFormat` (shared/tournament.ts). The result is written in the same statement that locks the date, guarded on `format_source` and on no sign-up having changed since the count (else "look again").
5. After the lock: an alert card (the site's `.ac`, X dismiss kept per player in the phone's memory, key = tournament + date pick + player) above the ticket card: "The Cold Open is scheduled for Thu Dec 17." and "Most players voted Americano." (or just "Format: Locked doubles" for a tie or a hand change). The ticket card's format line is back in the usual style. No player ever gets another player's vote or any count. The organizer's card shows "Locked 3, Americano 6, Either 2" and "Decided by the most votes / the tie rule / Changed by you". A hand change of the format (allowed until players hold tickets) sets the source to 'admin' and the alert keeps its key and says only the format. A re-pick or a Reschedule then a pick counts again and shows a fresh alert; once players hold tickets the format stays.
6. "~7:30 PM" while the date is TBD, the plain time after.
History: a `tournament_format` line (who or what decided it, with the counts).

### Where it differs from the brief (the code is the truth)
- `format_source` has a third value, 'tie' (decided by the tie rule), next to 'vote' and 'admin', so the alert can drop the vote claim without any extra read. NULL means the organizer chose the format when creating it (no vote was ever open). (Pass 2: every tournament gets the date alert; only a real vote majority says "Most players voted".)
- While the vote is open `format` holds the placeholder 'doubles' (the CHECK on the column); no screen shows it.
- Counts on the organizer's card are the votes of the players on the list now: every one of them before a date, then those who can make the picked date. A player who backs out after the lock drops out of the count.
- TBD and the vote rows also end after a Reschedule that players hold tickets on (they bought that format); a Reschedule nobody bought into goes back to TBD and the next pick counts again.
- The preview's calm profile now opens with NO tournament (so Create can be tapped); `--zip56` and `--zip55` build the older starts. The older seeds create their Winter Classic with an explicit Locked doubles format.
- The brief's PR title and branch name: the build system pins the branch to `claude/new-session-hnlsro`; no PR was opened (none was asked for).

### Review
A fresh independent reviewer read the whole change. Found and fixed: Edit settings after a Reschedule (with a player holding a ticket) was refused because an unchanged format was read as a hand change; and the vote count was not atomic with the date lock (now guarded). Confirmed fine: no vote or count reaches any player (answers, stamp, errors, History); the View as and backup copies carry raw rows only to the organizer; rule and previous-tournament lookup; races. Kept as is: the "~7:30 PM" shows for every tournament with no date, including old ones.

## Zip 62: Make the admin and player screens fast again (🎾62.speed), Wed Nov 18, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-6jer9k` (the session is named "🎾62.speed"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `4c427ab` (Zip 60
live, TOURNAMENTS switched on for everyone by Alex, The Cold Open visible). Same switch and the per-tournament Who can see it. **NO database
change** (no table, no column, no index, no migration). Nothing looks or behaves differently: only when things arrive changes.

### Measured first (before any change)
How: (1) the real server code on a local copy of the preview's calm fake world with "Fewer database trips" on as on live, counting every
database trip per answer (all trips in these handlers run one after another); (2) the same code deployed as a preview (fake database,
`pickleball-preview`, region ENAM like live), timed from this machine, which Cloudflare serves from Chicago (ORD), median of 9; (3) a real
browser on that preview with a warm cache, as a returning phone; (4) live, read only, no PIN: public answers and Cloudflare's own analytics.

| Screen (preview, fake data) | Switch OFF | ON, vote open | ON, tickets open (6 paid) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Admin load (dashboard) | 1.28 s, 33 trips | 1.33 s, 38 trips | 1.56 s, 43 trips |
| Admin 5-second check | 0.21 s, 3 | 0.26 s, 5 | 0.33 s, 7 |
| Player Home (Parker, on the list) | 0.41 s, 9 | 0.59 s, 13 | 0.59 s, 15 |
| Player Home (Vic, not on the list) | 0.40 s, 9 | 0.53 s, 13 | 0.69 s, 17 |
| Player 5-second check | 0.23 s, 4 | 0.29 to 0.31 s, 6 | 0.32 to 0.35 s, 7 to 8 |

Requests and order (browser, warm cache): the admin page asks one thing at open, the dashboard, after its files (from the cache); then one
check every 5 seconds. The "as of" copy showed at 0.07 s; fresh data drew 1.10 s (OFF) and 1.33 s (ON) after the open. The player page asks
/api/status and /api/group side by side; with the switch on, the card's own file (`TournamentHome`) was only asked for AFTER /api/group came
back, then the dark placeholder showed, then the real card exactly 0.30 s after the fresh games (React holds a placeholder at least 300 ms once
it shows one; this happened even with the file in the cache). On 4G (100 ms, 9 Mbps) the same: card 0.84 s after the first (saved copy) card.
Bytes: dashboard 49 KB, player Home 9 KB, checks 24 bytes, the card's file 23 KB (7 KB compressed).
Live, read only: one database trip costs about 40 ms (a 6-trip public answer 0.40 s against 0.15 s for one with none); D1's own time per
query is tiny (half under 0.3 ms); in the hour Alex switched it on, live answers took about 1 second on average, and 1.5 to 3.3 seconds at
1:20 to 1:25 PM Eastern, with 3 answers the phone gave up on. The per-query log showed the player tournament read at about 220 rows each and
the Hidden tournaments list at about 420 (both reading the whole task list), on every 5-second check.

### The cause (plain words)
With the switch on, every screen read the tournament one step at a time: its row, then its sign-ups, then its tickets, then the organizer's
player, each a separate trip to the database, in a row (about 40 ms each on live). The 5-second checks did all of it on every check, and the
full answers did it TWICE (once for the "did anything change?" fingerprint, once for the answer), plus one more trip for the Hidden
tournaments list. On the player page the card's file was fetched only after the games answer, and then React's minimum placeholder time
added 0.3 s. Nothing new runs on the 5-minute clock (checked: `server/tasks.ts` has no tournament work; the clock Worker only puts the four
tournament tables in Sunday's backup). No query was slow inside the database, so no index was needed.

### What changed
1. `server/stamp.ts`: the fingerprint's one batch carries the tournament reads too (only while the switch is on for that phone; off, the batch
   is exactly main's): the row, and through a subquery that picks the SAME tournament (the same WHERE and ORDER BY, ending on the id, in the
   same batch), its sign-ups and tickets, the organizer's player (the saved one, or every player when the organizer is found by the name in
   Settings), and for a player's card the freed-spot count (after Pay by) and what a cancel gave back (a canceled card) (`playerTourReads`,
   `adminTourReads` in `server/tournament.ts`). On an Only me tournament a phone without the organizer's own sign-in cookie reads none of its
   rows beyond the one that says it is Only me.
2. The views are built from those rows with no trip of their own, and the full answers (`dashboard`, `groupView`) send the view their own
   fingerprint built instead of building it again. Not reused (built again exactly as before): View as, a phone whose player is inactive, a
   build that hit an error, and a build that tried one of the two writes a read can make (a piece 1 date pick opening tickets, a hold coming back
   after the night), so a change that landed in between is what the answer shows, as before. The two look-only databases keep the old reads
   entirely ("Pretend it's...", whose batches answer nothing at all, and the read-only PIN's), so their answers are exactly what they were.
3. The dashboard's Hidden tournaments list and the tournament names on ticket credit lines join the shared trip ("Fewer database trips"
   prefetch) while the switch is on; off, exactly main's.
4. The Hidden check (`notHiddenSql`) names "no game" and the kind list the way the existing `task_log_once` index is written, so SQLite looks
   the one mark up instead of reading every task_log row (same answer: a hide mark never has a game).
5. Player page: a phone whose last answer had a card remembers it (`pb_tour_seen`) and starts the card's file the moment the page opens
   (usually from its cache), side by side with the games answer; a card whose file is already here is drawn directly, in the same moment as
   the rest of Home, with no placeholder. The first look on a phone works as before; a style file that failed is fetched again before the
   card is drawn (as the organizer file's loader does), so a weak signal can only mean no card until a reload, as before, never a card
   without its look. The organizer's phone starts the
   file once the dashboard has a tournament, so View as draws the card at once too. The file is still its own download; a phone that never
   had a card fetches nothing; styles are byte for byte the same files.
6. Preview only: Tournament test stage "Speed check (like live)" (The Cold Open on Everyone, the vote open, 9 on the list).

### After (same preview, same stages)
| Screen (preview, fake data) | Switch OFF | ON, vote open | ON, tickets open (6 paid) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Admin load (dashboard) | 1.19 s, 33 trips | 1.21 s, 33 trips | 1.34 s, 33 trips |
| Admin 5-second check | 0.19 s, 3 | 0.20 s, 3 | 0.20 s, 3 |
| Player Home (Parker) | 0.43 s, 9 | 0.40 s, 9 | 0.43 s, 9 |
| Player Home (Vic) | 0.43 s, 9 | 0.41 s, 9 | 0.41 s, 9 |
| Player 5-second check | 0.21 to 0.23 s, 4 | 0.22 to 0.24 s, 4 | 0.23 to 0.24 s, 4 |
The live-like Speed check stage, same rows, switch off then on: admin load 1.22 s / 1.23 s, admin check 0.19 / 0.20 s, player Home 0.41 /
0.38 to 0.41 s, checks 0.21 to 0.24 s either way. Browser, warm cache: the card's file comes from the cache at 0.05 s, the games answer lands at
0.45 s and the real card is drawn in that same moment (0 ms after the fresh games, no placeholder); on 4G the same. Admin fresh data about
1.2 to 1.4 s after the open (the dashboard's own 33 trips: the same with the switch off).

### Where it differs from the brief (the code is the truth)
- No TEST SPEED RULES section exists in SITE_RULES (neither copy); the usual unit and browser runs were used.
- The brief says the Players tab: the organizer's Players tab has no tournament part (it reads nothing new); the pop-in was the player's own

  organizer's in-browser copy, so it costs no network trip). Without "Fewer database trips" (not live) the Hidden list and the ticket names
  are their own trip, as before.

  Hidden games; about 40 ms per hidden game on live; 10 on the preview, which hides its empty games). A question below.

findings, all fixed with a test each: three states still cost one read on their own (after Pay by, a canceled card, an organizer found by
name), now in the same trip; a style file that failed at page open could have let a retry draw the card without its look (now fetched
again first); the old-way test proved less than it said (it now checks that the old way reads the row on its own and the single trip never
does, and the proof against main is committed as e2e/zip62-same.cjs); Only me rows were read for phones that can never see them (now
skipped); the row read and the pick now end their order on the id, so they provably pick the same tournament. Found during the build: "Pretend
it's..." answers every batch with nothing, so the look-only databases keep the old reads. A second pass on those fixes (it ran main's code
and this code on 31 states, 9 of its own: the organizer found by name, a saved organizer player that is gone, two players with the
organizer's name, Only me with a canceled Everyone one behind it): nothing serious left, 0 answers different. Its one low point is fixed: the
card's loader fetches failed style files again only after a failed try, so it never waits on another file's style (the organizer's phone
fetches the organizer file in the background).

### How the style is stored (no new column)
`tournaments.format` is the style in play; `format_source` says why: 'vote', 'tie', 'admin', NULL as before, plus `odd:<ISO time>` (switched to
Americano for an odd count) and `back:<ISO time>` (the organizer switched back). The time makes each switch its own banner and card. Older code
reads both as "the organizer's own" (sourceOf returns null), so a code rollback is safe.

## Zip 57: Tournaments, piece 3: teams, the schedule, game day, standings (🎾57.tourney3), Thu Nov 19, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-gfcgy1` (the session is named "🎾57.tourney3"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `316ac36` (Zip 64
and its part 8 live). Same switch, TOURNAMENTS, and the per-tournament Who can see it. **Database change: migration `0027_tournament_games`**
(two NEW tables, three NEW nullable columns; nothing existing changed). Applied to the fake preview database only. **NOT on live: the brief says
show Alex the change first.** No money moves anywhere in this piece. Piece 4 (ties, the wheel, End tournament, medals, credit) is NOT built.

### The database change (for Alex's OK)
- `ALTER TABLE tournaments ADD COLUMN teams_at TEXT;` (teams published), `court_numbers TEXT` (the venue's numbers, `[9,10]`), `paused_at TEXT`.
- `tournament_teams`: one row per Locked doubles team (seat 1 to 8, name, the two players with ON DELETE SET NULL, pool A or B, out_at when a team
  sits out during the night, changed_at when a partner changed after publishing). Foreign key to the tournament ON DELETE CASCADE.
- `tournament_games`: one row per game, made at Publish (round, court 1 or 2, stage pool / semi / final / third, pool, who plays as slots: 'T3' a
  team, 'A1' a place in a pool, 'W12' the winner of a game; play_to 11 / 9 / 7; claim (a team's We won), disputed_at, winner, result_by,
  skipped; seat_a and seat_b, the teams a result was given for). ON DELETE CASCADE.
- Undo (only to remove piece 3's data): `DROP TABLE tournament_games; DROP TABLE tournament_teams;` and the three `ALTER TABLE tournaments DROP
  COLUMN`. Code from before Zip 57 never reads any of it: a code rollback needs no database step.

### What it does
1. The game plan (shared/tournamentPlan.ts), the single source of truth from the zip's GAME_PLAN_TABLE.md: one pure function (players, courts,
   court minutes, style) gives the rounds, the length of pool or round robin games (11, 9 or 7: the longest that fits in the court time minus 10
   minutes; playoffs always to 11), the minutes used and whether it fits; Americano by its own rule (everyone at least 4 games). Every row of the
   table is a unit test (96 cells). The starting suggestion (`suggestedPlan`, shared/tournament.ts) now covers 6 to 16: 14 and 16 are 2 courts,
   3 hours, 7:00 PM (PLANS, smartPlan and the plan line read it; the old "14 and 16 stay the 12-player plan" is gone).
2. Finalize (mocks 60 and 61): a Courts row (1 | 2, saved in the existing `courts` field, 2 to start) under Plays, and one line under the rows:
   "Fits 12 players. Pool games to 11, done about 8:55 PM." (accent) or "Too tight for 12 players on 1 court. Use 2 courts or add court time."
   (amber). The count is who can make that date; under 6 it says so. Finalize is never blocked. Zip 64 part 8's "Plan:" line on the sheet gave
   way to this line (it fits the one Air screen: checked at 420 x 912). After Finalize the organizer card's Plan line, its cost and the "Call the
   venue" card use the chosen courts and the real hours.
3. When tickets close (Pay by), with the players really locked in: an amber card when it no longer fits, when a court is no longer needed (7 or
   fewer on 2 courts) or under 6 ("Cancel or reschedule?"; the buttons are on the tournament card below).
4. Draft teams (mock 15; Locked doubles, an even count of 6 to 16, after Pay by): strongest paired with weakest, each team's total, Swap (pick
   one of the team's two, then anyone on another team: both new totals shown), tap a team to rename it, Redo the draw (another pairing at most
   0.2 worse than the best one found), Publish teams. Publish balances the pools by team total (A, B, B, A ...), makes every game, and players
   see their partner and team only then. After publishing, before any result: Edit teams (back to the draft); a back out or a late join that
   leaves the teams out of step shows "Teams need a change." with Pair them (left-over players paired by closest level, published again; both
   players get "Your new partner is ..."); a whole team leaving gives one fewer team (byes). The courts' numbers (the site's court map) on the
   published card.
5. The schedule (shared/tournamentSchedule.ts `schedule`, pure, every size tested): 6 players: 3 games one at a time then the Final; 8: round
   robin in 3 rounds on 2 courts (courts swap each round) then Final and 3rd place; 10: 5 rounds, one team sits each round (each exactly once);
   12: two pools of 3, semifinals (pool winner vs the other pool's runner-up), Final and 3rd place; 14: Pool A of 4 and Pool B of 3, 5 rounds
   (Pool A uses both courts when Pool B is done); 16: two pools of 4, one game per pool per round, 6 rounds. On 1 court every game is one after
   another (the pools take turns), with no 3rd place game.
6. Game night, players (mocks 16 to 19, 51 to 53): before the night, under the ticket: Your team, Your games (each with its court, tappable to
   the court map once the courts are set; the Final "If you finish in the top 2"), All teams; with pools, Pool A and Pool B (where each team
   plays round 1, or Sits) and The night's times (shifted by the real start). On the night the short card (the name, "Game 1 of 3" or "Pool play
   · Round 1 of 3", a slim bar) takes the ticket's place; Game 1 "Begins at 7:30 PM" with We won and "<other team> won"; We won collapses to
   "<team> won Game 1" with Undo for 5 seconds, then it is sent and counts at once; the other team gets "Did you win?" (Yes, they won / No, we
   won); Up next; the Time check; Your games (done gray on green, next on blue); Standings (wins, then head to head) or the pools; Currently
   playing. Only their own games; names only (no levels: a question below).
7. Game night, the organizer (mocks 48 to 50, for Locked doubles: who won, no scores): the round's results (Done, Waiting with Confirm,
   Disputed, Playing with Set), Fix any game (a winner, or clear it), All games, the Time check with one tap ("Play to 9 from Round 2"), Pause
   (players see "Paused"), Player left (swap in a player locked in on no team or a paid standby player; or the team sits out its later games).
8. Time check (smart timing): rounds of 23 / 19 / 16 minutes; a round that ended late pushes the rest; when the night would end after the courts
   close minus 10 minutes it suggests games to 9 from the latest round that is enough, else to 7, else to 7 from the first round that can change
   ("That still runs about 9 minutes over."). A round with a result is never changed; playoffs never are. Players see the words once applied.
9. A back out after publishing that makes the count odd: zip 64's own switch to Americano (its Telegram, History line and amber card); its card
   now has "Copy text for the group" (who backed out, the date, $16, pay by 3 hours before the start, the site's address). An Americano night
   shows no teams (zip 61 builds that night).

  added to the preview database, which already had 0027): fixing a pool game later never moves a played semifinal or Final to other teams.

## Zip 61: Tournaments, the Americano night (🎾61.americano), Thu Nov 19, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-j4d3lq` (the session is named "🎾61.americano"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `77c57e2` (Zip 57
live, plus 🎾67's pre-check notes). Same switch, TOURNAMENTS, and the per-tournament Who can see it; no new switch. **Database change: migration
`0028_americano_scores`** (three NEW nullable columns on `tournament_games`: `score_a`, `score_b`, `claim_by`; nothing existing changed). Applied
to the fake preview database only. **NOT on live: Alex's OK first.** No money moves anywhere in this piece. The ending (awards, medals, ticker,
End tournament) is zip 58 and is NOT built.

### The database change (for Alex's OK)
- `ALTER TABLE tournament_games ADD COLUMN score_a INTEGER; ... score_b INTEGER; ... claim_by TEXT;`
- An Americano game is a `tournament_games` row like a Locked doubles one, with two players a side: `slot_a` / `slot_b` hold "id1+id2". The
  points each side scored go in `score_a` / `score_b`; `claim_by` is the player who entered the score waiting for the other side (on a skipped
  game, the player who left). The existing columns keep their zip 57 meaning (claim, disputed_at, winner, skipped).
- Undo (only to remove the scores): the three `ALTER TABLE tournament_games DROP COLUMN`. Code from before Zip 61 never reads them: a code
  rollback needs no database step.

### What it does
1. The schedule (shared/americanoSchedule.ts `americanoNight(players, courts, minutes, key)`, pure). Rounds and game length come only from the
   game plan table (shared/tournamentPlan.ts `americanoPlan`, zip 57). Players on court = 4 x the smaller of (courts, players / 4); the rest sit.
   Who sits: always the players who have sat least (sit-outs differ by at most 1 after every round). Partners: never again while an unused
   partner is left. Opponents spread evenly (every row of the table: the most two players meet is at most 2 more than the least; 8 players on 2
   courts for 3 hours is a perfect "whist" night: every partner once, every opponent exactly twice). Courts rotate (nobody with 3 or more games
   plays them all on one court). The pattern is searched once, offline (`npx vite-node scripts/americano-patterns.ts`), and saved for 6 to 16
   players, 1 or 2 courts, 16 rounds (shared/americanoPatterns.ts); a longer night carries on with the same rules. The players are put in the
   seats in an order drawn from the tournament's id, so the same list always gets the same rounds and nothing heavy runs on a screen refresh.
2. When the rows are written: never by a screen that only reads. Until the night's first save (a score, or the organizer's Fix, Time check or
   Player left) every screen works the rounds out from who is locked in, so a back out or a style switch before the night simply gives the new
   rounds. The first save writes every game (guarded: two saves at once write them once).
3. Players (pictures 31 to 37): before the night, Your rounds under zip 66's ticket (Round 4 "Break"). From 30 minutes before the start the
   night takes the ticket's place on Home: the hero ("Round 3 of 6"), the big VS card ("Round 3 · Court 1", "You + Parker" VS "Quinn +
   Reese", Enter score), or the dark break card ("Round 4 · Your break", "On break until Round 5", who else sits); the Time check; Your rounds
   (done green with Won or Lost, next blue); Standings (rank, name, wins-losses, points chip, your row highlighted); Currently playing (the other
   court; every court on a break); Show future games.
4. Enter score: zip 57's sheet, "Final score", each side with − and + (44 px; the number can also be typed), Submit score. Then zip 57's motion
   (the one copy, now `useHeldResult` in src/tournament/GameDayView.tsx): a win lights our side lime with the check and "✓ Let's go!"; a loss
   gives the winners a soft white glow (white at 16%, a 2 px white ring at 35%), dims our side, and the button says "Onto the next!"; about a
   second later the card slides to the next round (or the break card); the banner "You + Parker won 11 to 8" (or "Quinn + Reese won 11 to 8")
   with Undo and the 5 second drain line; sent after 5 seconds unless Undo (leaving Home still sends it). Reduced motion: no glow, no slide.
   The same loss motion now runs on Locked doubles' "<other team> won" (Alex, Nov 19).
5. The other side: "Is this right?" / "Vic says Round 3 ended 11 to 8 for Vic + Parker." / Yes, that's right / No, fix it. No, fix it opens the
   score sheet with the numbers from their side; their score replaces it (it counts) and the side that entered first is asked. The same score
   entered by both sides counts as a Yes.
6. The points table (Alex's answer, Nov 19): while everyone has played the same number of games, wins first, then total points; whenever
   players have played different numbers of games (a sit-out or someone left), win percentage first, then total points. Players still level
   when every game is in: "Tied" (and an amber card tells the organizer who).
7. The organizer: before the night the Rounds card ("10 locked in. 6 rounds to 11, 2 sit each round. New partner every round.", the courts'
   numbers, All rounds with who sits). On the night: zip 57's hero, Pause, the Time check (counted in rounds; never the last round), "Round 3 ·
   Scores" (Done, Waiting with Confirm, Changed, Playing with Set; "Waiting 7 min" or "8 min over" when late; a late score from an earlier round
   shows here too), Fix with two numbers (Save, Clear the score), All rounds, Player left (their games still to play are off; the others in them
   sit and get "Zoe left. Your Round 5 game is off."). A player who backs out during the night is handled the same way.
8. The switch: zip 64 decides the style (odd count at Pay by or after a back out). An Americano night shows its rounds from the moment tickets
   close; players see zip 64's "Tournament style is now Americano." and their rounds. Switch back (zip 64's button) gives zip 57's teams again.
   Mid-night: zip 64 never switches after the start; and Switch back is refused once an Americano score is in ("The rounds have started.").

### Where it differs from the brief (the code is the truth)
- The Round 3 preview stage: "a score waiting" is the other court's ROUND 2 score (late, with Confirm on the organizer's card), so Round 3 is
  on both courts and Currently playing shows the other court as picture 32 draws it.
- Ranking: Alex chose win percentage whenever game counts differ (then total points), so mid-night after a sit-out round the table can differ
  from picture 32's order (a 1-0 player who sat Round 1 is above 1-1 players).
- 8 players on 2 courts: everyone plays every round with a new partner, so the courts cannot also be even: over 7 rounds one player can have 6
  games on one court. Partners and opponents are kept perfect instead (every partner once, every opponent twice).
- Scores are whole numbers 0 to 30 and cannot be equal; "first to 11" is not enforced (a game cut short by time can end 9 to 7).

### Review
A fresh independent reviewer (no part in the build) read the whole change. Its real findings, each fixed with a test (tests/zip61-day.test.ts,
"the independent review, each finding"):
- A stale Yes could confirm a score the screen never showed (taken back and entered again in between): Yes and No, fix it now send the score
  the screen showed, and a different one says "The score just changed. Look again."
- A partner's different score silently replaced the one waiting: now refused (the same score is fine).
- A later round's score was accepted, and an open score sheet could jump to the next round on a refresh: the server takes only the round being
  played ("Round 5 has not started. Finish Round 1 first."), the key is required, and the sheet holds the round it was opened for.
- The "left" note's key carried the leaver's player id: now a short hash (every key of every player's answer is checked for ids).
- The leaver's own header fell back to "Round 1 of 6": it follows the night now.
- Player left could wipe a score entered a moment before: it only skips games still exactly as read.
- Player left with nothing left to play said "is out": it says "had no games left" and changes nothing.
- Organizer taps (Fix, Time check, Player left) before the night would write the rows early: they open 15 minutes before the start, like the
  players' scores.
Not changed (by design): one round's missing score holds Enter score on the next round (rounds are played together; the organizer sees it as
late and can Set it).

### What it does (the brief's twelve things)
1. Ties for a playoff place, every structure (round robin to the Final, pools to the semifinals, 6 to 16): standings now split teams level on wins
   by head to head again inside any part still level, so two tied teams are always settled by the game they played. Three in a circle: the wheel.
   A tie only counts when its places lead to different games (shared/tournamentSchedule.ts placeClasses; 1st and 2nd level before a Final between
   1st and 2nd is no tie). Shape 'ab' (it decides the top place, or every place): Game A (the two not picked), then Game B (A's winner against the
   bye team); order winner of B, loser of B, loser of A. Shape 'a' (two of the three go on to the same game): Game A only; the bye team and A's
   winner go on. Both to 5, in the first playoff round, on the first free court; the semis, the Final and 3rd place then fill in by themselves.
   The team with the best record outside the tie (same group) spins on their phone; none (a whole pool tied): the organizer. The organizer can
   always spin too (a phone may be dead). Four or more tied (or two that never played): the organizer taps one team per place until the places
   left lead to the same game. A team that left: before the spin it drops out of the tie (head to head among the rest); after the spin the tie
   stays and its game is a walkover. A pool result fixed after the spin sets the tie's games aside (kept; they come back if the tie does).
2. The wheel (src/tournament/parts.tsx Wheel, shared by both screens): three slices, the arrow on the rim at the top, the server's answer (crypto
   random) stored in tournament_ties, about 4 seconds clockwise slowing down, the winning slice lit and the others dimmed; reduced motion: no spin.
   Phones that did not see the spin play it once (spun in the last 3 minutes); a reload shows the same answer, no spin.
3. The Final and 3rd place: unchanged (57's). Added: "Also now · Court 2 · 3rd place" under a finalist's Final card; the Playoff card during a
   tie (Game A, Game B, then the games it feeds: "Winner of B vs Kitchen Crew", "Losers of A and B", "Same time as the final").
4. End tournament (organizer Home, once the Final or every Americano round is in): the slim bar, "Final is done / Net Ninjas won / Vic + Wren beat
   Kitchen Crew (Rowan + Zoe)." (Americano: "Round 6 is done / Vic finished first / Parker was second."), then the End tournament card (rows, Edit
   awards, Confirm winners and end). It replaces the round results, Pause and Player left. An I paid still waiting blocks it (the card says so).
5. Credit: one credit_ledger 'kept' row per award, no game, reason 'tour:<id>:champion' or ':second' (shared/credit.ts: "$14 Tournament champion,
   The Cold Open"). Granted once: one batch, every write guarded on a fresh end key; the unique index refuses a second award row. $0 skips it.
   The organizer gets the medal, never credit (the site's rule: the organizer holds no credit); the card says "Alex: medal only".
6. Medals (src/Medals.tsx, the main download): next to the name at the top of Home and after names on game cards; 1 to 3 stacked, from 4 one medal
   and "×N". Permanent, counted across tournaments everyone could see. The ticker and the congratulations card are their own small file.
7. Saved for later (tournament_results): finish, record, Americano points, team and partner, the picked and approved level (organizer only).
8. Ticker (full width, slim, runs right to left, still with reduced motion) for the banner length; the congratulations card with Nice, once.
9. Edit awards: Change (teams, or 1st and 2nd), the credit amounts (whole dollars, $0 allowed), banner 1 to 4 weeks, Save.
10. 3rd place after a tie: the losers of A and B (a round robin's P3 and P4 come from the tie's order). One court: no 3rd place game (57's rule).
11. History > Tournaments (third chip, only while the switch is on): Tournament history and Wins by player; hidden tournaments stay out.
12. Hide and restore: unchanged (only canceled tournaments can be hidden; History lists ended ones only, and filters hidden ones too).
After End: status 'ended'. openById and playerTarget find nothing open, so every organizer tap and every player tap on its games, teams, results
and tickets answers "look again" / "not open"; the result writes also check the tournament is still open when they land. Unused standby holds come
back as credit at End (as they would at 10 PM). Home has no tournament card, no live view and no "Show future games" any more.

## Zip 68: Make the organizer's Home fast (🎾68.speed), Thu Nov 19, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-0k1imm` (the session is named "🎾68.speed"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `40d0f32` (Zips 57,
58, 61, 66 live; main equals live). **NO database change** (no table, column, index or migration). **Nothing looks or behaves differently**: no
money, ticket, credit or tournament rule is touched; only how many times the server goes to the database while building the organizer's Home.

### Measured first (before any change)
How: (1) the real server code on local copies of the preview's fake worlds (the calm one, and the full one with three months of finalized
games, money and a cash out pending), with "Fewer database trips" on as on live, counting every trip and listing it (`scripts/zip68-admin-speed.ts`,
`SEQ=1`); (2) main's code deployed as the preview address `zip68-before` and timed from this machine (Cloudflare serves it from Chicago, like
Alex's phone), median of 15 to 21 calls (`e2e/zip68-time.cjs`); (3) a real browser on that preview, on 4G and with a warm cache
(`admin-net.cjs`, scratch); (4) Cloudflare's own numbers for live (read only, no player data).
- The 73 trips in the brief are the count with "Fewer database trips" OFF. Live has it ON: the dashboard made 33 trips (calm world) or 26 (full
  world; 30 with Venue alert, Acting for others, Second Chance and hidden games on), all one after another; the 5-second check made 3.
- On Cloudflare (main's code): dashboard 1.18 to 1.30 s at tickets open, all locked in, game day and game night; the check 128 to 140 ms.
- Where the trips came from: 1 sign-in check, 1 read of the switch rows, 1 fingerprint batch, 1 "next weeks' games" check, 1 shared prefetch,
  1 money picture, then about 17 single reads one after another (hidden players, Spent's three reads, venue charges, hidden games, the venue
  card, Acting for others, this month's games, hidden early games, the organizer's player, the Do this now marks, the alert settings, the
  smart alerts row, the organizer motion row a second time, Second Chance marks, every game for Hidden games, the month counts), then one read
  PER HIDDEN GAME (10 on the calm preview), and one batch per finalized game check. No slow query: D1's own time is 0.3 ms per query (live,
  Nov 12 to 19); every trip costs about 35 to 40 ms of travel, so the count is the time.
- Live, Nov 17 to 19 (all requests, not only the organizer's; Cloudflare does not split by address): typical 0.3 s, slowest 10% about 1.1 s,
  slowest 1% about 2.9 s (4.7 s in the busiest hour). The browser on 4G: after any deploy (new file names, nothing cached) the page spends
  about 2 s downloading its code, then waits 1.2 s for the dashboard: 3.3 s and more. With a warm cache, 1.4 s, almost all of it the dashboard.
  That is the "sometimes 3 to 4 seconds": the first open after a deploy, or a slower network moment multiplied by 33 trips in a row.

### What changed
1. `server/speed.ts`: two small pieces on the "Fewer database trips" wrapper. `firstWithSwitches`: the organizer sign-in check and the
   read of every switch row in ONE trip (the first switch question then uses those rows; a write in between, a failed batch, the switch off
   after deciding, or a look-only database fall back to exactly the old reads).
   `isFast`: whether the shared trips are on for this request.
2. `server/auth.ts` `requireAdmin`: uses `firstWithSwitches` (every organizer call saves one trip, the 5-second check included).
3. `server/admin.ts` `dashboard`: with the switch on, ONE shared trip carries the fingerprint's reads, the "next weeks' games" check and every
   read of the screen that does not wait on another (`dashboardReads`, the same reads in the order the screen asks them); the existing finalized
   game check trip also carries each hidden game's players and the Second Chance marks. The answers are the database's own; a read the screen
   asks that was not sent early (or any read after a write, like the weekly upkeep adding a game) goes to the database on its own, as before.
4. Each read the list names is now written once, as an exported read (`plannedStartsRead`, `cancelChargesRead`, `hiddenSessionsRead`,
   `adminHiddenPlayersRead`, `adminHiddenGamesRead`, `venueAlertReads`, `taggedLinesRead`, `playedCountsRead`/`monthPlayedRead`, `marksRead`,
   `smartAlertsOffRead`, `alertRowRead`, `requestPlayersRead`, `secondChanceMarksRead`, `adminStampReads`), used by its own function too, so
   the list can never drift from the real query (a drift would only cost a trip, never change an answer).
5. Not changed: the player screens, every tap, the clock, the 5-second check's own work, the payload (same bytes).

   spots taken are back to 8 or more, every kept drop gets its credit back once, by the usual back-out statements, in the same batch that filled
   the spot (`releaseKeptStatements`, appended to every batch that can fill a spot: `fillSpotsStatements`). The keep decision is made inside the
   statement that takes the player off the list (`lateDropKeepsSql`), from the rows as they are when it lands. A Cancel gives kept money back; the
   end of the night (unused holds), End tournament and the organizer's I paid answers never do. Drop out closes 3 hours before the start (server:
   409 "Drop out has closed. Text Alex."; the card hides it). The Drop out sheet's two lines show only when the rule applies (`dropKeeps`).

  follows. The venue card shows again with the new times. Players on the list: "The Cold Open now ends at 9:30 PM (was 10 PM)." / "Based on the
  number of players locked in.", dismissed per phone; "was" is the time before the first move they were told about; moving back removes it.

### 2. One tie rule (shared/tournamentSchedule.ts `standings` / `settle`)
Wins; then head to head, only when exactly 2 teams are level and they played; then point difference; then points scored; teams still level
after a split go through the same steps again (so two left level after point difference are settled by their game); teams level on all of it
are "Tied": the wheel (three) or the organizer's picks (four or more). Pools use it inside each pool. It is THE function behind the players'
Standings, Alex's night screen (resolveGames, the tie cards), the semifinal / Final / 3rd place seeding, End tournament (doublesOutcome; across
pools: wins, then point difference, then points scored) and so History, and the test stages. Americano is unchanged (wins, win % when game
counts differ, then total points).

statuses (a score saved before Zip 71 counts as done). The dead drain-line banner option (`drain` in src/ui.tsx and its style) is removed. The
test stages and their descriptions say Enter score. No Telegram alert carries a game result. The DB columns `claim` and `disputed_at` stay (old
rows only; dropping them needs a migration). The "claim" words still in admin code are the money "I paid" answers, not game results.

## Zip 76: Money fixes from the 🎾75 audit, tournament money on Totals (🎾76.money fixes), Fri Nov 20, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-82pe3u` (the session is named "🎾76.money fixes"; the build system pins the branch name). Built on main `85989f8` (Zip 74
live, main equal to live). **NO database change**: no table, column or migration. No new switch: every change is a fix, a rule Alex decided, or
the Totals change he approved (it rides the Tournaments switch, on for everyone on live). The Cold Open's settings, tickets and money untouched.

### MUST 1: late drop credit (the 🎾75 audit)
- `OPEN_FEE` / `OPEN_LATE_DROP` (server/lateFees.ts) were NULL, not false, on a late drop that did not leave the game short (`played` stays
  NULL), so `NOT OPEN_FEE` skipped the seat: the organizer's "Paid" on that player's unconfirmed I paid said "$14 is credit now" and gave $0.
  Now `COALESCE(played, -1) = 0` and the whole fee test is COALESCEd to 0. Tests: tests/late-fees.test.ts (Paid gives the $14 once; Didn't
  pay leaves nothing owed), and the 576-shape agreement test now checks OPEN_FEE and NOT OPEN_FEE as real 0 and 1 (it compared `=== 1`, so
  NULL passed). Both new tests fail on the old code.
- Live, read-only (Fri Nov 20): no late drop exists at all on live (0 rows with late_drop_at), so no seat is stuck.

### MUST 2: Drop out words
- Late, already paid: "It's past the 7:00 AM cancel-by. Your $14 stays on this game unless someone takes your spot." (never "you still owe");
  a host with a guest the same ("Your $28 stays on this game unless someone takes your 2 spots."). A plain drop adds the toast's money line:
  "Your spot opens up for someone else. $14 comes back as credit." (an I paid waiting: "Your $14 comes back as credit once Alex confirms your
  payment."). shared/lateFees.ts, shared/guestSpot.ts, shared/credit.ts dropMoneyLine, src/pages/PlayerHome.tsx.

### Tournament money on Totals (pictures totals-pair-1 to 5)
- server/money.ts `tournamentsOf`: each tournament ENDED with its night in the month: tickets (credit and confirmed cash still on the tickets)
  minus courts (court rate x courts x the final hours) minus the award credit rows = its result. One read, in place of Zip 56's "Tournament
  tickets" line (gone). `handCreditOf`: credit added by hand (Adjust credit) minus taken away, a cost in the month given (from the ledger the
  page already reads).
- So far: "<name> tournament", made money "−$8" green, cost money "$10" red; only after End tournament. Projected: the same once ended, before
  that the open tournament's "You make if it fills" (the dashboard's money line, no new read) when its night is in that month. A tap opens
  Tickets / Courts / Prizes in place (no caret), a second tap closes. "Credit you added (by hand)" shows only when not $0.
- Running total: "Tournaments <n>" (net), in Out of pocket and Average per month; per game and $/court stay regular games only (hand credit
  counts there). Month by month: "6 games · 1 tournament".
- Tests: tests/zip76-totals.test.ts (picture 5 to the cent: Dec $58 at $11/court, Jan $52 at $21/court, Feb $48 at $16/court; Running
  total $90 + $66 + $2 = $158, $53 a month, $14 a game; hand credit balances; on the real server a 10 player night: $160 - $120 - $28 = +$12,
  nothing before End, nothing with Tournaments off).

### Tournament rules
- The late drop keep rule counts locked in the way players see it (lockedInSql: spots and whole-ticket I paids still waiting), and a dropper
  whose whole-ticket I paid waits can be kept (the Venmo payer is held to the credit payer's rule). Giving kept money back still needs paid
  spots (refilledSql), so an I paid that turns out unpaid never releases anyone.
- Pay by moved later (past now): every drop kept under the old Pay by comes back as credit in the same batch (releaseKeptStatements with
  payByMovedLaterSql; one History line each, once).
- Venue hours still never apply to tournaments: left for the smart venue hours work.
- Tests: tests/zip70-time.test.ts "Zip 76" (3; all fail on the old code).

### Small rules and clicks
- Full regular game (no waitlist, 12 in): the card shows a disabled "Full" (view `atLimit`), not an I'm in that always fails.
