## Zip 77: Americano hidden standings and the standings reveal, plus game night fixes (🎾77.reveal), Fri Nov 20, 2026
Branch `claude/new-session-qt8af3` (the session is named "🎾77.reveal"). Built on main `85989f8` (Zip 74 live), then rebased onto `4610c01`
(🎾76 live, as the brief asks: 🎾76 ships first; two small conflicts, the preview's calm start and the size budget). Same switch, TOURNAMENTS (on for
everyone on live); no new switch (every tournament zip since 57 rides it). **NO database change**: no table, column or migration. The reveal's
clock is the existing `tournaments.ended_at` (End already writes it at the tap).

### 1. During the night (picture 1)
- `server/americanoDay.ts` playerRoundsView takes a mode: 'hidden' (every player: `standings: []`, `standingsHidden`, the table is never built
  for them), 'live' (the organizer's own player on the organizer's own signed-in phone, or View as of that player: he catches wrong scores
  there), 'final' (after the reveal). The sign-in check rides the player batch (`playerTourReads` adds one admin_sessions read only for a phone
  with an organizer cookie; `adminCookieHash`), so the organizer's own Home makes no extra trip (tests/zip62-speed).
- Player screen: no Standings card at all; one centered muted line at the bottom ("Standings will be revealed at the end of the night.").
  Your rounds and Currently playing unchanged. Locked doubles unchanged.

### 2. All games in (picture 2)
- `waiting` on the day view (every game in, on the night, not revealed): the card loses its kicker, the bar becomes a 3 px white 16% divider
  (`DoneHero`), and the slim green "Final standings coming soon" card with three Pickleball components bouncing in turn takes the Up next
  card's place (`WaitingCard`). One line from 390 px (font `clamp`), wraps between words below that.
- While it shows, Home checks every 2 seconds whatever the phone is doing (`LivePoller.setFast`, `useLiveUpdates({ fastMs })`); only then,
  and not forever: 30 minutes without a touch stops it like any other check (`FAST_STOP_MS`), in case the reveal never comes that night.

### 3. Alex's side
- The End card's button on an Americano night reads "Reveal standings" (`data-tm-reveal`); the same `awardsAction 'end'` (credit once, history,
  medals, banner). No confirm step (End had none). Toast "Revealing on every phone". Alex's own screens keep everything as before.

### 4. The reveal (picture 3, the video)
- `shared/reveal.ts`: one timeline from the number of players. T0 = tap + 3 s. Countdown 0 to 5 s, slots at 5 s, last place at 6 s, then the
  brief's gaps (10 players: exactly the mock's 6.0, 7.5, 9.0, 10.6, 12.2, 13.8, 15.6, 17.8, 20.4, 24.6; drumrolls 19.7 and 22.6; X at 27.4). 9
  players: about 29 s from the tap. Below 7th 1.5 s apart, 1.0 s with more than 10.
- The server: an Americano tournament ended in the last 6 hours reaches the players who were in it (`ACTIVE_WHERE` + `shownRevealed`, worked
  out from the existing ?2 cutoff with strftime; open tournaments first), as status 'ended' with `reveal { tapMs, players }` and the board's
  rows from `tournament_results` (Edit awards' 1st and 2nd win; names, records, points only). Nothing on it can be tapped: sign-up, Edit
  sign-up and Back out answer "not open" (`playerTarget` refuses 'ended').
- The phone (`src/tournament/Reveal.tsx`, its own CSS `reveal.css`, in the tournament chunk): every frame is a pure function of T on the
  SERVER's clock (`/api/group/version` now answers `t`; each check is a reading, the shortest round trip wins; `src/serverClock.ts`). The
  tournament card itself grows open (0.55 s), "Final standings" at the name's size 16 px under the divider, rows slide up with a lime flash,
  3rd a small pop and one ring, 2nd a 0.7 s drumroll and a drop with a ring and sparks, 1st a 2 s faster drumroll, the flight, the card's
  shake, lime rays, a double shock wave, sparks, the lime row and the site's GOLD medal (`MedalIcon`, now exported from src/Medals.tsx) with a
  dashed ring that spins and settles. No confetti, no silver or bronze, no money. YOU on the viewer's row. Names wrap between words (a
  container query gives them room at 320).
- Mid-join lands on the same frame; a phone that opens after it finished sees the final board once (`pb_reveal_seen:<id>`, storage wrapped);
  the X folds the board away and the night's final standings sit in the Standings card (no Live chip).
- The hold: until REVEAL_HOLD_MS (about 36 s, the 16 player board) after the tap, nothing at the top of Home tells the winner: no ticker, no
  congratulations, no medals (`withoutRevealing`), and the award credit is left out of the player's credit chip and history (display only:
  the credit itself is granted at the tap, as before). The change stamp carries the awards, so the hold's end is a change and phones reload.
- Reduced motion: the same order and timing; fades only (no slide, fly, shake, rays, sparks or waves).
- Speed: nothing new on the organizer's Home or its refresh.

### 5. Game night fixes (the 🎾75 audit)
- Back closes sheets (`src/backStack.ts`): every open layer (Sheet, so ConfirmDialog too, and the court map) owns one history entry; Back
  pops it and closes the top layer; a layer closed any other way gives its entry back with history.go; entries are only counted, so a sheet
  handing over to the next reuses one. Organizer tabs: each switch is one entry; Back returns to the last tab with its scroll spot.
- Up next card: the gradient's top `#2b8c5b` -> `#1f7049` (lime 4.74:1, white 6.05:1 at the very top) and the players line 92% white.
- 44 px taps: the Court link's `::before` (44 px tall), the card's Edit, Drop out, Who's in and the row Drop out at 44 px.
- The organizer's sheet on a game with no result: "Set Game 1 · Court 1" / "Set · Round 6 · Court 2" (Fix once it has one). 11 to 0 start kept.

### Review
A fresh reviewer (no part in the build) read the diff. Fixed: (1) the sign-up routes still reached the revealed night for 6 hours (a History
line, no money): refused now; (2) the 2 second check had no end: 30 quiet minutes now, and setting it wakes a page that had stopped; (3) two
new tests were flaky (the organizer placing 1st gets no credit; a break round has no score): fixed, 3 runs in a row green; (4) the medal hold
took one off a public count for an Only me night: only public nights now; (5) the revealed card forced `today`, folding the week's game cards
for 6 hours: `today` keeps its own window and the card shows the reveal regardless; (6) Back's guard for a slow history.go is 2.5 s (was
0.8 s). Kept, as designed: the first answer after the tap carries the board's whole order (every phone needs it to jump in mid-reveal); the
screens hold everything that tells the winner. The version's `t` is the request's own time (a later reading breaks the byte-for-byte speed
tests; the few ms bias is the same on every phone).

## Zip 80: leftovers before Dec 1: fair sit-outs, safety checks, small fixes (🎾80.leftovers), Sat Nov 21, 2026

Built on main `d1b8f9f` (Zip 79 live, deployment e4f3eab1). Branch `claude/new-session-fy1hug`. **No migration.** No new switch: the
tournament pieces ride Tournaments (on for everyone on live), the rest are fixes. The clock Worker changes (a backup copy after End).
The Cold Open's settings, tickets and money untouched.

### 1. Fair sit-outs
- Americano (shared/americanoSchedule.ts `sitLimit`, shared/americanoPatterns.ts regenerated by scripts/americano-patterns.ts with its
  searches in scripts/americano-patterns-lib.ts): nobody sits more than 2 rounds in a row on 2 courts (8 to 16) and on 1 court up to 10;
  sit-outs differ by at most 1; no partner repeats while one is unused; nights past 16 rounds (`extendRounds`) keep the limit. On 1 court only
  4 play a round, so 11 to 16 cannot all be 2 (12 could, but only by the same three foursomes all night; 13 to 16 never): 11 to 13 sit at
  most 3, 14 to 16 at most 4: the least that keeps the opponent mix at least as good as before (at 3, 14 and 15 make opponent pairs meet twice
  from round 7). Only these 9 saved patterns changed: 9:4, 10:4, 11:4, 12:4, 13:4, 14:4, 15:4, 16:4 (1 court) and 15:8; every other size is
  rebuilt byte for byte as before.
- Most sits in a row before -> after: 9 (1 court) 3 -> 2, 10 (1 court) 3 -> 2, 15 (2 courts) 3 -> 2, 11 (1c) 4 -> 3, 12 (1c) 4 -> 3,
  13 (1c) 5 -> 3, 14 (1c) 5 -> 4, 15 (1c) 6 -> 4, 16 (1c) 6 -> 4. Pairs who meet as opponents twice or more, before -> after, at real
  night lengths: 9 (1c) 9/13/17 -> 3/6/12 at 9/10/12 rounds; 11 (1c) 5/8 -> 0/0 at 11/12; 12 (1c) 6/8/11 -> 2/3/3; 13 (1c) 6 -> 0 at 13;
  14 to 16 (1c) 0 through 16 rounds; 15 (2c) 3/5/9 -> 1/3/8 at 10/11/12 (court balance as good or better at every length from 4). One cost:
  10 on 1 court at 10 rounds 6 -> 7 (11 rounds 9 = 9, 12 rounds 12 -> 10); an exhaustive check proved 2 in a row cannot keep opponents unique
  at 5 rounds for 10 (4 for 11), the lengths of a night too short to fit.
- Locked doubles, 14 players on 2 courts (shared/tournamentSchedule.ts FOURTEEN_TWO_COURTS, the only order of its kind, every order tried):
  r1 Pool A on both courts, r2 to r4 a Pool A game beside a Pool B game (Pool B on Court 2), r5 one Pool A game. Most games in a row 3 -> 2
  (counting the semifinal), most sits in a row 3 -> 2. Every other size as before (only 3 teams, 4 teams on 2 courts, 5 on 2 and a group of
  3 on 2 courts play 3 or more in a row, as any order must).
- The Cold Open (9 or 10 on 2 courts: 9:8 and 10:8) was already fair (1 and 2 in a row) and is unchanged.

### 2. Tie time
- A tie's Game A and Game B (to 5) are stored with the first playoff round's number and were counted as nothing. Now (shared/tournamentPlan.ts
  TIE_MINUTES = 13, the 16/19/23 steps carried down to 5; shared/tournamentSchedule.ts `tiesEnd`, `tieGamesAhead`; server/tournamentDay.ts):
  they are played as soon as the wheel spins on a free court, and the playoff round starts when both the pools before it and the tie games
  are done (their last result, else now + 13 minutes a game on the busiest court). The Time check and the players' night times
  ("Semifinals about 9:10 PM") follow; a tie's minutes read as time behind; shorter pool games are suggested only when they would help.

### 3. Safety checks
- `credit_back_twice` (scripts/integrity-checks.sql, now 22 columns): a seat's live payment can never have more back above the final price
  (finalized, not_played) since it was paid than the payment; a settled seat (refunded) can never have a money-back row after the one that
  settled it. "After" is strictly later (a drop and a rejoin in one instant are fine). `tour_credit_back_twice` (the tournament file, 14):
  a money-back row on a ticket made after its current payment while it still holds money. The extra time file already caught it
  (ext_credit_not_ledger; proved). tests/zip80-double-credit.test.ts: real flows (pay, drop, rejoin, pay again, drop again; a cancel; a
  back out) read 0, seeded doubles read 1; the ledger fuzz runs the check after every step of 360 random walks (no false alarm).
- Restore test: the plain `npm run restore-test` checks all three kinds of backup: the newest weekly copy, the newest SQL export saved at a
  deploy (new: read with plain SELECTs, loaded, saved as a Settings > Backup file, restored, every value compared; `-- --export [id]` alone),
  and a fresh export of live as a Settings > Backup file and as a weekly copy.
- A backup copy after End tournament / Reveal standings: the clock Worker (worker/backup.ts planCopy, `endedSince`): a tournament that
  ended after the newest copy (of any kind) counts as a copy asked for, made at the next hourly look ("2026-12-01-asked-2200"); live is only
  read. Needs the clock Worker deployed (this ship).
- The 401: Zips 58, 76 and 77 ran `wrangler r2 object put pickleball-backups/...`, treating `pickleball-backups` as an R2 bucket. It is a D1
  DATABASE (scripts/deploy-export.mjs saves there; Zips 74, 78, 79 used it and it worked). The API token has no R2 permission and there is no
  such bucket: 401 "Authentication error". Nothing to change in Cloudflare. New: `npm run backup:before-deploy -- "<what>"` (export, save,
  bookmark, delete the local copy, stop on any failure); docs/DEPLOY.md says it plainly.

## Zip 81: special venue hours (🎾81.venue hours), Fri Nov 20 to Sat Nov 21, 2026

Built on main `d1b8f9f` (Zip 79 live). Branch `claude/new-session-aenfpb`. No migration (the hours live in the group's settings_json, `venueHours`),
no Worker deploy, no money logic touched, nothing new for players. Rides the Booking hours switch (ON on live, read-only check Fri Nov 20).

### What it does (pictures 1 to 5)
- Settings > Schedule > "Special venue hours" under Usual game time: the hint ("Winter hours to Jan 31 · 5 holidays"; None when empty), Change.
- The sheet: "Normal: Mon to Sat 8 AM to 10 PM · Sun 8 AM to 7 PM"; the entries soonest first (a range: dates, then hours on the next line; one
  day: "Thu Nov 26 · 8 AM to noon", Closed in red); a tap opens a row in place with Edit and Remove (no caret), a second tap closes it; the green
  Add special hours; the quiet Change normal hours link (the fixed table is editable there, the same seven day rows).
- Add special hours: Name; Dates / One day. Dates: From, To, a start and end per weekday. One day: Date, Open (start and end) or Closed. Save.
- The rules (`shared/bookingHours.ts` dayRule): a one-day entry beats a range on its date; two ranges never overlap and two one-day entries never
  share a date (the save refuses it, `shared/venueHours.ts` readSpecial); an entry ends after its last date and leaves the list; no repeats.
  An end of 12:00 AM means midnight (a game may end exactly then).
- Where the hours are checked, all by the game's own date: Add game and Edit game (the Start grid only offers that date's times; a closed day says
  so; the server refuses with the old words plus the entry's name: "The venue is open 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM on this day (Thanksgiving). Pick times
  inside those hours." / "The venue is closed on this day (Christmas). Pick another date."), the usual time (against the normal Tue and Thu),
  Second Chance start times (`shared/secondChanceTimes.ts`), and tournaments: Finalize and moving the start or end after Finalize
  (server/tournament.ts enforceTournamentHours; the Finalize and Time boxes show the same line and keep the button off).
- Conflicts (picture 5): organizer Home, at the very top, one amber card per game still to come (not canceled, not finalized) and the finalized
  tournament outside its date's hours: "Thu Nov 26: the venue closes at noon." / "Your 8 PM game is after that." (starts before closing: "ends
  after that"; opens later: "the venue opens at ..."; closed: "Fri Dec 25: the venue is closed." / "Your 8 PM game is that day."). Cancel game
  opens the usual Cancel flow; the tournament's Change time opens its card with the Time row. Worked out on the phone from Home's own data.
- The holiday "hours confirmed?" question is skipped when a one-day entry covers that date (the holiday's name stays).
- Saves: POST /api/admin/venue-hours/special, POST /api/admin/venue-hours/remove, PUT /api/admin/venue-hours/normal (server/venueHours.ts), one
  guarded write each; the general Settings save takes venueHours from the row at the moment it writes, so it never undoes an hours save.

## 🎾88.rolling courts (Tue Nov 24, 2026; LIVE 11:05 PM Eastern, after 🎾86 round 2 and 🎾87)

### What changed (the code is the truth; SITE_RULES "Rolling courts and the night card (Zip 88)")
1. THE RULE (shared/rollingCourts.ts `rollCourts`, pure): when a court frees up, the earliest game still to play whose players are all free and
   at their own next game starts there; a semifinal waits for every pool game, the Final and 3rd place for every semifinal too; a tie's game
   from the wheel's spin (its row's created_at). Replayed every read from the schedule order and `result_at` (nothing stored, no migration).
   Fix and Clear keep `result_at` (COALESCE); a skipped game that is cleared gets none (it is to play). Player left skips keep an earlier one.
2. Americano (server/americanoDay.ts amFacts) and Locked doubles (server/tournamentDay.ts facts) read the replay: a game's court once it is
   on one (null on the phones before), `onNow` = on a court, Currently playing = the courts now, the break card ends when the next game starts,
   the late flag from the game's own start. Both views send `courtsNow` and `sittingNow`; Locked doubles also `standings` (each group's table).
   Players' and the organizer's scores for a game not on a court: 409 "That game is not on a court yet." (was "Finish Round N first").
3. The night card (src/pages/admin/NightCard.tsx, nightCardData.ts, night-card88.css): pictures 1 to 3. Replaces the green banner, the scores
   box and (Tournament.tsx `nightCardUp`) the folded tournament card on the night; the admin week row hides on the night (Admin.tsx). Pause and
   Player left ask "Are you sure?" (inline Yes / No; Resume asks nothing). All rounds opens at a tapped bar (Scoreboard `focusRound`). End card:
   "Set prizes first" (red) above the button while no prize is set.
4. Stages (THIS_ZIP): zip88_rd3 (start here, picture 1), zip88_early (picture 2 as a LOOK on the test page: 10 names can never start a round
   early; Home gets zip88_rd3), zip88_final (picture 3; the Final and 3rd place rows set to 7 for the look: the real Time check never shortens
   playoffs), zip88_sitting (Vic sits Round 4).

5. Alex's two additions. START NOW: server/tournament.ts START_TASK, `nightStartMs` (the planned start or the tap, whichever is first: every
   "has the night started" asks it: amFacts, facts, the score gates, the live windows, the Time/Plan lock), `startNowOpen`; the column
   `started_early` rides SHOWN_SQL, ACTIVE_FOR_PLAYER_SQL and activeTournament (same statements); POST .../games { action: 'start' }
   (server/tournamentDay.ts startNow, guarded insert, audit 'tournament_started_now'); AdminTournamentView.startNow / startedEarly; the
   card's Start now button and its "Are you sure?" (src/pages/admin/Tournament.tsx HomeCard, night-card88.css); nightOnAt follows the tap.
   TEAM NAMES: server/tournamentDay.ts teamHasScore (canRename and playerTeamName); src/tournament/GameDayView.tsx keeps Your team on the night
   while canRename. Stage zip88_ready "Game day: ready to start now".

6. Alex's preview round. SAVED COURTS: shared/rollingCourts.ts `pin` (a saved game goes on its court at its moment; a game the rule had put
   there steps back off), PIN_PREFIX / pinOf / pinText / claimTime; saveAmericanoCourts (server/americanoDay.ts) and saveDoublesCourts
   (server/tournamentDay.ts) write court + claim_at 'on:<ISO>' for every started, unsaved game, before and after every write of the night
   (scores, Fix, Clear, Player left, the wheel, Start now; Tickets' Take off), updated_at untouched; every score write keeps claim_at; the Time
   check reads claimTime (never a saved court). salesClosed counts Start now (Take off and Drop out close then too). GAMES START SOON:
   PlayerRoundsView / PlayerDayView `startsSoon` (game day, not started), src/tournament/Reveal.tsx WaitingCard (title, sub) and
   StartsSoonCard (serverNow, 1 s ticks in the last 30 minutes), shared/reveal.ts countdownText; stage zip88_soon "Player: 20 minutes before
   start".

### Finding (told Alex, he left it to my judgment: ship the rule as written)
On 8 to 10 player nights (both styles) the fair schedule always has someone of every later game still on the other court, so a freed court never
finds a game it may start: courts wait exactly as before, The Cold Open plays as lockstep did. Early starts happen on 11 to 16 player Americano
and Locked doubles groups nights (12 to 16). Night lengths with Court 1 always faster (pure simulation, minutes): 8: 104 vs lockstep 104; 9: 104/104;
10: 104/104; 11: 102/104; 12: 105/104 (a game moved to the slower court can cost a minute).

### Review (a fresh reviewer, no part in the build)
Fixed: (1) a semifinal whose teams were known lost its court when a tie's wheel was spun later (the playoffs waited for the tie games too);
(2) a game skipped by a team leaving, then cleared, could never be scored again; (3) a cleared score on a waiting court's last game read "Off,
Done" and counted as in; (4) a bar went purple from a skipped game; (5) duplicate keys on the sitting balls; an unused prop. Kept and noted:
the replay works from today's state, so a player taken off the list mid-night (no longer locked in) or a cleared pool score during the semis
moved the courts as if it had always been so: FIXED in Alex's round (saved courts); the "8 min over" late words show in All rounds only.
